descriptionChirho: To physically lift or raise something upward, including raising one's voice, lifting eyes, or lifting up stones; emphasizes upward directional movement rather than acquisition or removal.
To take up or pick up an object from where it lies, including picking up a bed or mat, gathering leftover fragments, or taking up serpents; focuses on acquiring possession of something at hand.
To carry or bear a load such as a cross, burden, or person; emphasizes sustained transport rather than the initial act of picking up, as evidenced by Arabic حَمَلَ and Swahili beba.

To take away, remove, or deprive someone of something, whether physically removing an object, pruning branches, taking away sin, or carrying someone off; the multilingual glosses consistently use removal vocabulary (Arabic يَنْزِعُ, Swahili ondoa, Korean 빼앗다/제거하다).
An emphatic demand for the removal or destruction of a person, characteristically the crowd's cry 'Away with him!' demanding crucifixion (John 19:15, Acts 21:36); Arabic أَزِلْهُ, Swahili Mwondoeni.
Passive forms expressing being taken away or removed, whether of things, privileges, or obstacles; distinct from 'be lifted up' in that the focus is on loss or separation rather than elevation.
A nautical technical term meaning to hoist up the anchor and set sail, used in Acts 27:13 and 27:17; evidenced by Spanish habiendo-levado-anclas and Korean 닻을-올리고.

An idiomatic expression τὴν ψυχὴν ἡμῶν αἴρεις meaning 'you keep us in suspense' or 'you hold our soul/life in the balance' (John 10:24); Spanish tienes-en-suspenso confirms the figurative sense distinct from all physical meanings.
